name: In-Process Circuit Breaker
strategy: State machine (Closed -> Open -> Half-Open). Fail fast when downstream is degraded to prevent local thread exhaustion.
pitfalls: Setting threshold too low (flapping breaker); neglecting fallback strategy or monitoring metrics
canonical_snippet: type State = 'CLOSED' | 'OPEN' | 'HALF_OPEN'; if (state === 'OPEN') throw new CircuitOpenError();

name: Exponential Backoff with Jitter
strategy: Exponentially increase delay between retries and add full or decorrelated random jitter to de-synchronize callers.
pitfalls: Retrying non-idempotent mutations (POST payments); retrying without jitter causing coordinated stampedes
canonical_snippet: sleep = min(max_delay, base_delay * 2^attempt); actual_delay = random_between(0, sleep)

name: Bulkhead Semaphore
strategy: Isolate concurrent execution slots per downstream dependency using bounded semaphores.
pitfalls: Single unbounded concurrency pool allowing one slow microservice to exhaust entire host resources
canonical_snippet: semaphore = new Semaphore(max_concurrent_calls); try { await semaphore.acquire() } finally { semaphore.release() }

name: Token Bucket Rate Limiter
strategy: Maintain a bucket with capacity N tokens, refilled at rate R tokens/sec. Operations consume 1 token; reject when empty.
pitfalls: Using unsynchronized floats in concurrent multi-threaded environments without atomic operations
canonical_snippet: tokens = min(capacity, tokens + (now - last_refill) * rate); if (tokens >= 1) { tokens -= 1; allow(); }

name: Timeout and Context Cancellation
strategy: Attach an explicit deadline or cancellation context to every async task and check cancellation periodically.
pitfalls: Forgetting to check context cancellation inside tight CPU loops; ignoring context.Done() in Go/Python
canonical_snippet: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(parentCtx, 3*time.Second); defer cancel(); select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() }

name: Bounded Worker Pool
strategy: Spawn a fixed number of N worker goroutines/threads reading from a bounded channel or queue with graceful drain.
pitfalls: Spawning unbounded goroutines per incoming HTTP request leading to OOM crash under load
canonical_snippet: func worker(jobs <-chan Job) { for j := range jobs { process(j) } }

name: Structured Concurrency (TaskGroup)
failure_mode: Orphaned background tasks / silent unhandled exceptions
strategy: Scope concurrent child tasks to a lexical block (TaskGroup in Python, errgroup in Go). If one fails, cancel siblings.
pitfalls: Fire-and-forget background tasks that continue running after caller HTTP request timed out
canonical_snippet: async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: task1 = tg.create_task(fetch1()); task2 = tg.create_task(fetch2())
